name: Bexarotene
lead: Bexarotene (Targretin) is an oral and topical retinoid that selectively activates retinoid X receptors (RXRs). It is FDA-approved for the skin manifestations of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, where it is used to improve skin lesions.[11][4]

In appearance communities it is discussed as a retinoid-class compound, but its documented use is medical: treatment of refractory cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, including mycosis fungoides.[3] Clearing or flattening skin plaques is the visible result in that setting.[4]
The US label carries a boxed warning for birth defects, and common effects include raised blood lipids and central hypothyroidism.[11][4]

chain: Regulates skin cell growth and differentiation
Lymphoma skin plaques flatten or clear
angle.text: Bexarotene is prescribed to improve skin lesions of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Trials reported reduced plaque elevation, and a small psoriasis study found improved severity with oral use.

infobox: Rx-only; boxed warning for birth defects

paras: The oral capsule is indicated for cutaneous manifestations of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma (CTCL) in patients refractory to at least one prior systemic therapy.[11] A topical gel was cleared in 2000 for early-stage CTCL skin lesions.[5] Mycosis fungoides, the most common CTCL subtype, may be treated with oral bexarotene after skin-directed therapies.[3] Bexarotene has also been a comparator in the ALCANZA trial.[6]

In refractory or persistent early-stage CTCL, the overall response rate was 54% with oral bexarotene; in advanced-stage disease it was 45%.[4] Topical bexarotene produced response rates of 44% to 63% in early-stage CTCL in separate trials.[4] A multinational phase II-III trial in refractory advanced CTCL enrolled 94 patients.[7] In psoriasis, oral bexarotene reduced plaque elevation and severity in a trial summarized in a review.[4] In ALCANZA, bexarotene or methotrexate was the physician's-choice arm against brentuximab vedotin.[6]

The most common adverse events with oral bexarotene are elevated triglycerides and cholesterol, central hypothyroidism and headache; reversible pancreatitis has been reported.[4] The drug suppresses TSH and free thyroxine, and is listed among causes of drug-induced central hypothyroidism.[2] The label lists hyperlipidemia, pancreatitis, liver toxicity, hypothyroidism, neutropenia and cataracts as warnings, and contraindicates pregnancy because of birth defects.[11]

Bexarotene binds RXR alpha, beta and gamma, which pair with partners including retinoic acid receptors, the vitamin D receptor, thyroid receptor and PPARs to regulate gene expression for differentiation and proliferation.[11][4]
Bexarotene (LGD-1069) from Ligand was the first RXR-selective retinoid to enter clinical trials; Targretin capsules launched in the US in January 2000 for CTCL.[5]
Bexarotene has been studied in lung, breast and other cancers, schizophrenia and Alzheimer's disease models.[10][9][8]

timeline.event: FDA approves Targretin capsules for CTCL.[5]

card.summary: A prescription RXR-selective retinoid that improves skin lesions in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
card.note: Boxed warning for birth defects; raises lipids and can cause hypothyroidism.

quick.overview:
Bexarotene (Targretin) is a prescription retinoid taken as a capsule or applied as a gel. It is approved for the skin lesions of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.

In trials, about half of people with early-stage disease responded, with plaques becoming flatter and clearer.
quick.mechanism: It activates retinoid X receptors, which partner with other nuclear receptors to regulate cell growth and differentiation.
quick.risks: Common effects are high triglycerides and cholesterol, central hypothyroidism and headache. The label has a boxed warning for birth defects. It is Rx-only.
